steps.name: Load counts/metadata, QC profile, and flag shallow sample
steps.question: What do the RSEM expected-count matrix (12000 genes x 12 samples) and metadata (12 samples, condition treated/control) look like after loading, and does sample_01's library size (~4x below median) show library-size-driven distortion (rank correlation with other samples, PCA outlier position, fraction of zero/low-count genes) consistent with a shallow/degraded sample versus a true biological low-responder?
acceptance_criteria: Counts and metadata are loaded and joined on sample ID with the treated/control label from metadata.csv confirmed for all 12 samples
Per-sample library size, gene detection rate, and count distribution are reported, with sample_01 quantified relative to the other 11
A sample-level PCA or hierarchical clustering on variance-stabilized/log-normalized counts is produced and sample_01's position relative to its condition group is reported

Report states explicitly whether sample_01 appears as a technical outlier (isolated on PCA, disproportionate low-count gene fraction) versus a plausible biological data point, without deciding exclusion at this step

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression, treated vs control, primary run (all 12 samples)
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes are differentially expressed between the 6 treated and 6 control colon samples using DESeq2 on the RSEM expected counts (rounded to integers, as no effective-length matrix was delivered to enable length-scaled tximport import)?
acceptance_criteria: RSEM expected counts are rounded to nearest integer before DESeqDataSetFromMatrix, and this rounding step (a compromise forced by the missing genes.results/effective-length files) is stated in the output
Design is ~condition with condition releveled so control is the reference level, unpaired two-group contrast, single batch (no batch term needed per design)
Standard DESeq2 filtering (rows with all-zero or near-zero counts removed pre-test), size-factor normalization via median-of-ratios, and Wald test are applied
apeglm (or ashr as fallback if apeglm errors on this design) is used for log2FoldChange shrinkage; the shrinkage method actually used is reported
Full results table (gene, baseMean, log2FoldChange, shrunken LFC, p-value, padj) is output for all tested genes, with genes at padj < 0.05 counted and listed separately
Independent filtering summary and dispersion plot are reported for diagnostic purposes

steps.name: Sensitivity re-run excluding sample_01
steps.question: Does the treated-vs-control DE result change materially when the shallow-library sample_01 is excluded (11 samples, arms unbalanced by one sample) — which genes lose or gain significance, and how correlated are the two log2FoldChange vectors?
acceptance_criteria: Same DESeq2 pipeline (rounding, filtering, size factors, Wald test, apeglm/ashr shrinkage) is rerun on the 11-sample matrix with sample_01 removed
Genes significant (padj < 0.05) in the full-cohort run (T1S2) but not in the sample_01-excluded run, and vice versa, are tabulated explicitly
Pearson/Spearman correlation of log2FoldChange between the two runs is reported across genes tested in both

Report states plainly whether the primary conclusion (which genes differ) is robust to sample_01's inclusion or is materially sample_01-dependent, without picking one run as 'the' answer unless the evidence clearly supports it

steps.name: Pathway enrichment on the DE gene list(s)
steps.question: Which WikiPathways, MSigDB Hallmark, and MSigDB GO Biological Process gene sets are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control colon samples (using the primary 12-sample DESeq2 result, and separately noting any change using the sample_01-excluded result if T1S3 showed material divergence)?
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment (over-representation test on padj<0.05 genes, or fgsea preranked on the full signed statistic/log2FoldChange list) is run against the human WikiPathways GMT, the human MSigDB Hallmark GMT, and the human MSigDB GO Biological Process GMT available in the reference store
Gene symbols in the DESeq2 results are matched to gene set member symbols; any mismatch/coverage rate is reported (e.g., fraction of tested genes found in each gene set collection)
Significant pathways (BH-adjusted p < 0.05 or the enrichment tool's default threshold) are reported per collection with directionality (which arm the pathway is enriched toward) stated
If T1S3 showed the DE list is sensitive to sample_01, enrichment is flagged as inheriting that instability rather than presented as independently robust

plan.title: Colon RSEM DE: 6 treated vs 6 control with QC gate
plan.analytical_narrative: The delivered matrix is RSEM gene-level expected counts (non-integer, 12000 genes x 12 samples) with no per-sample genes.results and thus no effective-length column, so tximport-style length-scaled correction cannot be reconstructed from what was delivered — the counts must be treated as gene-level counts and rounded for a count-based negative-binomial model, and this compromise is stated explicitly rather than concealed. Sample sample_01 has a library size about 4x below the median, which at n=6 per arm is a real risk of a single-sample-driven result; the plan does not exclude it a priori but runs the pipeline with and without it and reports whether findings depend on it, and profiles it independently for degradation/technical failure signatures before any exclusion decision. Design is unpaired, single batch, 6 vs 6 — a standard two-group DESeq2 contrast, gene-level, with independent filtering, apeglm shrinkage for effect sizes, and BH FDR. Downstream, DE results feed WikiPathways and MSigDB-hallmark/GO enrichment (both staged for human) using the organism-matched gene sets already confirmed present, giving pathway-level context for the treated-vs-control genes without inventing mechanism beyond what the enrichment supports.
